subject.title: [Feature]: Make detached longwork final delivery ownership explicit

question: Which first-class ownership model should OpenClaw use for detached longwork final delivery: an explicit owner-mode contract, a narrower extension of completionOwnerKey plus the delivery queue, or no new public surface?
rationale: Current main has partial internal routing and durable delivery state, but the public invariant, default compatibility behavior, and substrate ownership are product/API choices that automation cannot safely pick.

options.title: Extend existing delivery substrate
options.body: Add the smallest explicit owner signal to the current subagent run/delivery record and routing helpers, preserving current defaults while proving one full-final owner.

options.title: Add a broader owner-mode API
options.body: Sponsor a wider public completionOwner-style contract similar to the closed implementation PR, accepting the larger compatibility and documentation surface.

options.title: Treat current internals as sufficient
options.body: Close this direction only if maintainers decide completionOwnerKey plus pending delivery state already covers the product invariant without a public owner mode.

recommendation.title: Extend existing delivery substrate
recommendation.body: Add the smallest explicit owner signal to the current subagent run/delivery record and routing helpers, preserving current defaults while proving one full-final owner.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored and merged the latest current-main changes on the completion-owner and deferred-spawn steering surface.
